key_insight: RASP separates reading from learning: inference uses every LoRA atom, while training updates only a sparse subset within one fixed-size adapter.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support memory-constrained continual adaptation of engineering vision models, but constitutive modeling and solid-mechanics applications are not evaluated in the abstract.
method: Use a scene-modulated cosine router to select the top-q unlocked atoms for gradient updates while retaining all atoms during inference.
Penalize Gram coherence between updated and non-updated output directions to reduce interference.
Combine activation history and atom spectral norms into a consolidation index that controls step attenuation and boundary anchor locking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports matching or surpassing branch-expanding LoRA learners on CIFAR-100, CUB-200, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-A with a constant adapter parameter footprint.
watch_item: Long-horizon adaptation as atoms become locked remains a concern; the abstract provides no quantitative results or task-horizon details.
paper_title: RASP: Read-All, Sparse-Plasticity Continual Learning in a Stationary-Size LoRA
